headline: Acquisition-aware repositories and benchmarks reshape computational proteomics workflows
label: Proteomics Data Analysis Pipelines
summary: Expanding public top-down spectral resources and systematic DIA benchmarking now let proteomics tools be assessed against acquisition mode and platform.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational processing of MS data that depends on how spectra are acquired and organized. TopRepo provides over 12 million top-down spectra from 12 species, including a 5M-spectrum annotated library that supports proteoform search and deep learning-based spectral prediction. A systematic evaluation of low-input DIA workflows on an Astral mass spectrometer compares DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe, gradient conditions and quantification methods. A nanopore platform applies AI-driven analysis to single-molecule event streams for peptide differentiation, and iPepGen links DNA/RNA-seq neoantigen prediction with MS-based peptide verification and prioritization. CERTOMICS, a Nextflow single-cell multiomics pipeline with CAR-positive cell identification, extends the theme to a different data modality. What is new is the pairing of resource-scoped repositories with systematic benchmarking across acquisition modes and platforms.
